title: Merge
summary: git merge brings another branch's commits into your current branch, either by moving forward or with a merge commit.

levels.title: Fast-forward
levels.briefing: git merge <branch> brings that branch's work into the branch you are on. If your branch has no new commits of its own, git just moves it forward: a fast-forward. If both branches have new commits, git creates a merge commit with two parents.
levels.objective: The feature branch has a new commit. Merge it into main.

cheatsheet.description: Merge a branch into the current one
Move to the branch that should receive the work

hints: You are already on main, the branch that should receive the work.
git merge takes the name of the branch to bring in.
levels.successMessage: main had nothing new, so git fast-forwarded it to feature's commit. No merge commit was needed.

levels.title: A merge commit
levels.objective: main and feature both have new commits. Merge feature into main.
hints: The branches have split, so a fast-forward is not possible.
Merge as usual; git will make a merge commit.
levels.successMessage: The merge commit has two parents, joining both lines of work in the graph.

levels.title: Keep the history
levels.objective: Merge feature into main with a merge commit, even though a fast-forward is possible.
hints: A normal merge here would fast-forward.
There is a flag that turns the fast-forward off.
levels.successMessage: --no-ff keeps a visible record that the feature was developed on its own branch.

levels.title: Update a branch
levels.objective: main has moved on. Bring main's new commit into the feature branch.
hints: Merging always brings work into the branch you are on.
Switch to feature first, then merge main.
Run: git switch feature, then git merge main
levels.successMessage: Merging main into your branch keeps it up to date while you work.
